{{pagebanner|Tlahuac CDMX banner.jpg}}

'''Tláhuac''' is a borough of [[Mexico City]]. It is very different from the traditional tourist areas of the city and is regarded as an Off-the-Beaten-Path part of the city where only naturalists and those studying the [[Indigenous cultures of Mesoamerica|Iidigenous practices of pre-Hispanic cultures]] come to visit. Tláhuac is where a traveler interested in [[Day of the Dead]] traditions will find '''San Andrés Mixquic''', where a unique candlelit celebration is regarded as one of the oldest and most authentic celebrations. Tláhuac is one of the 16 ''alcaldias'' (boroughs) that make up CDMX. A poor choice for a first-time visitor, Tlahuac has some hidden gems that can be rewarding for a tenth trip to Mexico City as it reveals some of the city's hidden dimensions.

=== By bus ===
Tláhuac is served by several routes of the RTP bus service. All RTP routes through Tláhuac terminate at Metro Tláhuac, which is a transportation center for the area. No Metrobus routes serve Tláhuac.

=== Seven Native Towns ===
The '''Siete Pueblos Originarios de Tláhuac''' refers to seven indigenous villages making up Tlahuac that significantly pre-date the Spanish conquest. These villages areː

* '''San Andrés Mixquic''' - Most famous of the traditional villages due to its [[Day of the Dead]] traditions centered on candle-lit Night of the Dead ceremonies.
* '''San Pedro Tláhuac''' - Seat of local government, founded in the late 12th century on a small island between Lake Chalco and Lake Xochimilco. It features the grand Church of St. Peter the Apostle, built over an ancient ceremonial center.
* '''Santiago Zapotitlán''' - Once a lakeside town, the village is known for its community traditions, local carnivals, and cultural resistance against rapid urbanization
* '''San Francisco Tlaltenco''' - Settled long before the Aztec capital of Tenochtitlán, its name comes from Nahuatl words meaning "on the shore of the earth."  
* '''Santa Catarina Yechuizotl''' - Riverside community near the slopes of the Sierra de Santa Catarina, a series of dormant volcanoes.  
* '''San Nicolas Tetelco''' - Quiet, rural village where farming is still a way of life. 
* '''San Juan Ixtayopan''' - Rural farming community known for preserving cultural traditions but with no significant tourist sites.

=== Events ===
[[File:Día de muertos en Mixquic I.jpg|thumb|Día de Muertos in San Andres Mixquic]]
* '''Feria Regional de Tlahuac''' - held in late June each year, the celebration is the biggest festival of the year and honors Tlahuac's patron saint

* '''San Andrés Mixquic''' is a traditional village that is renowned as one of the most authentically unique celebrations of [[Day of the Dead]]. Visitors from around the country come for a serenely spectacular celebration on Night of the Dead when the village turns off all electric lights and people carry candles to  light their way to the village cemetery. This celebration is referred to as the ''Alumbrada''.
